text:
incident-bot: PAGER — P1 — Valencia Health (private VPC / dedicated pool) experiencing auth failures (401) on vpc-auth-proxy. Rate ~60/min. Possible OIDC/JWKS issue. Pager: https://pager.example/INC-8342 · runbook: https://playbook.local/vpc-oidc

oncall-ryan: Acked. Pulling logs and checking metrics.

alyssa: Quick skim of the logs shows repeated `kid not found in jwks`. Could be their IdP rotated keys and our JWKS cache hasn't picked it up. Which pool is affected?

oncall-ryan: It's the valencia-dedicated-01 pool, two gateway nodes (valencia-gw-1/2).

jason-engr: Confirming from ingress logs:
```
[2026-03-15T02:14:12Z] auth-proxy valencia-gw-1 ERROR jwt: failed to verify token: kid not found in jwks (kid=abc123)
[2026-03-15T02:14:12Z] upstream 10.2.1.5: GET /v1/resource -> 401
[2026-03-15T02:14:18Z] auth-proxy valencia-gw-2 ERROR jwt: failed to verify token: kid not found in jwks (kid=abc123)
```

alyssa: That looks like an IdP-side rotation where the new JWKS doesn't include the old kid (or tokens were minted with mismatched key). Our VPC proxies cache JWKS for 15m by default.

oncall-ryan: I'm going to try a cache flush and bounce the auth-proxy on gw-1 first.

oncall-ryan: SSHing into gw-1 and flushing cache:```
ssh runner@valencia-gw-1
sudo systemctl restart redwood-auth-proxy
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/internal/cache/flush | jq .
```

ops-bot: Restart task queued for valencia-gw-1 (task id task-7741).

oncall-ryan: Restart finished on gw-1, re-testing — still seeing 401s from gw-2 and some 502s upstream.

samir: If cache flush didn't help, maybe jwks endpoint responses are inconsistent across nodes (load-balancer). Can we curl their jwks from both gateways?

oncall-ryan: Good call. From gw-1:```
curl -sS https://idp.valencia-health.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq .keys | jq 'map(.kid)'
# -> ["def456","ghi789"]
```
From gw-2 (via its egress IP):```
curl -sS --interface eth0 https://idp.valencia-health.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq .keys | jq 'map(.kid)'
# -> ["def456"]
```

alyssa: Huh — gw-2 is seeing a JWKS without the kid expected by some tokens (abc123). That explains why some nodes accept tokens and some reject. Looks like an upstream replication / CDN inconsistency at their IdP.

maria-cs: Reached Valencia oncall (Ana). She says they rotated keys at 02:05 UTC and a subset of their JWKS endpoints are still propagating. They're contacting their IdP vendor and rolling back rotation if needed. Ana asks if we can do a temporary mitigation so their users aren't blocked.

jason-engr: Short-term mitigations we can consider: 1) lower JWKS cache TTL to 30s for the dedicated pool; 2) enable fallback to Redwood-hosted JWKS mirror (if present); 3) accept stale keys for short window (dangerous). Which is least risk?

security: We strongly prefer not to accept stale keys globally. Temporary allowlist for this customer only is ok if documented and timeboxed. Need approval from CS and Prod.

oncall-ryan: I can patch the valencia nodes with JWKS_TTL=30 and enable JWKS_FALLBACK=true for just that pool. Applying now to gw-1 and gw-2:```
# On control plane for valencia pool
redwoodctl pools patch valencia-dedicated-01 --set auth.jwks_ttl=30
redwoodctl pools patch valencia-dedicated-01 --set auth.jwks_fallback=true
```

ops-bot: Patch applied to valencia-dedicated-01 (change id change-992). Rolling restart scheduled for 2 nodes.

oncall-ryan: Rolling restart done. Testing auth endpoints — traffic success rate improving. Error rate down from 60/min to ~5/min.

maria-cs: Valencia oncall (Ana) confirms partial improvement for mobile app login flows. They're continuing rollback of their rotation and asking for a 10-minute stabilization window.

jason-engr: We're still seeing a handful of rejects from tokens signed with abc123 while some requests succeed (depending on gateway). Given customer is rolling back, keep TTL low and fallback on for 20 minutes, then revert.

security: Record this as an approved short-term exception: allowlist valencia pool JWKS_FALLBACK for 20m. Add ticket for postmortem and remediation.

ops-bot: Exception recorded in change-992 (expires 20m from now).

oncall-ryan: Monitoring. I'll keep the channel updated. Handing off to samir for next shift in 40m. Samir, you get the oncall.

samir: Taking over. Thanks Ryan. I'll keep an eye on metrics and the customer thread.

ana: (typo fix) — actually `ana-valencia-oncall` confirmed rollback complete at 02:36 UTC and they reissued tokens.

oncall-ryan: Verified after their rollback: all gateways returning 200 for auth and token verification. Error rates back to baseline.

incident-bot: RESOLVED — Valencia Health auth failures (INC-8342) resolved at 1935010375. Summary: customer key rotation + inconsistent JWKS propagation from IdP caused kid not found errors on some gateway nodes. Mitigation: flushed caches, reduced JWKS TTL to 30s for the pool, enabled hosted JWKS fallback for 20m, coordinated with customer to rollback rotation and reissue tokens.

security: Action items created: (1) add JWKS kid-mismatch alert to prod alerting (ALERT-457), (2) default JWKS TTL for VPC pools reduced to 60s (config change PR), (3) update VPC auth runbook with specific instructions to flush cache + enable fallback, (4) provide guidance to account teams to advise customers on staged key rotations.

maria-cs: I'll update the Valencia account ticket with the timeline and who we engaged. Customer is satisfied with the rollback and mitigation. :white_check_mark:

oncall-ryan: Filed incident note and added logs to the incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/local/INC-8342/notes

samir: I'll own the follow-ups and the postmortem doc. Passing to oncall queue.

security: Recommend a short audit to ensure no other pools using long JWKS TTLs.

ops-bot: Incident INC-8342 closed by oncall-ryan.

(emoji reactions throughout: :rotating_light:, :white_check_mark:, :lock:, :raised_hands:)
